name: Greenish bottle green
lede: Greenish bottle green is a deep, cool green carried into our library from the Japanese traditional color Aotake-iro, named for green bamboo, and it sits only 3.0 units from the plain [[bottle-green]].

sections.title: Aotake-iro, green bamboo
sections.body:
Our library lists this color under the Japanese name Aotake-iro, written 青竹色, glossed as "green bamboo color" [1]. No book consulted for this project independently dates the name beyond that gloss, so its coinage is undocumented here [1].

The library's swatch measures lightness 37, chroma 36 and hue 160 degrees, and it files under the Greens family, used chiefly in fashion and textile contexts [1]. At 3.0 color-distance units from [[bottle-green]], the two are close enough that most eyes would call them the same bottle green, and the library also flags [[spruce]] as a nearby neighbor [1]. Within this same batch of traditional names, [[grey-celadon]] and [[greenish-umber]] sit in neighboring hue families.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within range of this swatch appears in 8 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 0.03 percent, as photographed [2]. Half of its appearances sit in shadow areas, a quarter in mid-tones and a quarter in highlights [2]. The earliest dated match is T. Davies's *Ship in Full Sail*, 1827; the heaviest use we found is in Mary Susan Collins's 1929 *Primrose*, where it covers 29 percent of the canvas [2]. The archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor on the color's history, not a first sighting [2].
